summary:
A wire report (carried by Allwork.Space) on a global scramble to patch critical vulnerabilities in PHP, the programming language underpinning much of the web. Fixes were released Wednesday after the flaws, which had lurked for years, were uncovered using AI; maintainers urged users to update immediately. Details became public before fixes were ready, and exploitation attempts surged into the millions, per Cloudflare and Amazon.

Governments and companies took websites offline as a precaution, disrupting banking, airline, rail, tax and government services from Tokyo to Helsinki. Japanese organizations including Nomura, Mitsubishi UFJ, ANA, East Japan Railway, Asahi Group and Tokio Marine suspended some internet services; Japan's Ministry of Finance, Meteorological Agency and National Tax Agency partially or fully suspended online services. France's Orange suspended access to certain PHP-based sites across subsidiaries. Tencent Cloud urged customers to upgrade PHP but did not call for shutdowns. Finland's state IT provider Valtori patched overnight and gradually lifted precautionary blocks, warning restoration could take days or weeks because systems need careful testing; it said the outages were not caused by exploitation or a breach.

Several Asian governments ordered cybersecurity inspections. China's industry ministry urged system inspections, upgrades to the latest secure PHP version, stronger monitoring, and rotation of accounts, passwords and keys. South Korea raised its private-sector cyber alert level and activated emergency response.

Microsoft CEO Satya Nadella, speaking in Germany, said he had not seen anything like it in a long time and stressed building software that can be securely maintained as systems grow complex. Aikido Security co-founder Madeline Lawrence framed it as a race between defenders patching and attackers using AI to exploit. Bitkom security head Felix Kuhlenkamp said large operators had largely updated, but smaller organizations and complex systems may lag, especially sites on unsupported old PHP versions requiring full system updates.

claims.claim: Exploit attempts against the PHP flaws escalated rapidly around public disclosure
claims.stat: thousands of attempts in the 10 hours before announcement, tens of thousands within 45 minutes after, hundreds of thousands within 2 hours, millions subsequently
claims.attribution: Cloudflare CEO Matthew Prince, in a post on X

claims.claim: Amazon also observed widespread exploitation of the vulnerabilities
